items.sentence: FY2022 was the step change: revenue rose 17.1% to $28.7 billion on higher retail sales volumes and favorable weather .

passages.filing: FY2022 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: EU&I’s higher segment income is due to higher retail sales volumes and favorable weather, partially offset by higher depreciation and higher interest expense. The following is a detailed discussion of the variance drivers by line item.

items.label: partial

items.sentence: FY2020 was the trough, with net income down 63.3% to $1.4 billion on coal ash impairment charges and COVID-19 volume declines .

passages.filing: FY2020 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure’s variance is primarily due to impairment charges and revenue reductions related to the CCR settlement agreement filed with the NCUC to resolve coal ash cost recovery issues, unfavorable weather and lower volumes driven by impacts from the COVID-19 pandemic, partially offset by base rate adjustments in various jurisdictions. The following is a detailed discussion of the variance drivers by line item.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Coal ash impairments and COVID volumes explain the EU&I segment variance, not consolidated net income.

items.sentence: FY2024's 1.7pp margin gain came with net income up 59.2% to $4.5 billion, helped by rate increases and riders and by prior-year Commercial Renewables impairments .

passages.filing: FY2024 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Duke Energy's 2024 Net Income Available to Duke Energy Corporation (GAAP Reported Earnings) increased primarily due to higher impairments on the sale of the Commercial Renewables business in the prior year. Additional drivers primarily include growth from rate increases and riders, improved weather and higher sales volumes, partially offset by higher interest expense, depreciation on a growing asset base and storm costs, along with a higher effective tax rate. See “Results of Operations” below for a detailed discussion of the consolidated results of operations and a detailed discussion of financial results for each of Duke Energy’s reportable business segments, as well as Other.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P18 names prior-year Commercial Renewables impairments and rate increases and riders as net income drivers.

items.sentence: FY2022 operating cash flow fell 28.5% to $5.9 billion as rising fuel costs created undercollections financed with borrowings .

passages.filing: FY2022 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: As a result of rapidly rising commodity costs, including natural gas, fuel and purchased power prices in excess of amounts included in fuel-related revenues has led to an increase in the undercollection of fuel costs from customers at certain jurisdictions including Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress and Duke Energy Florida. These amounts have been deferred in regulatory assets and have impacted the cash flows of the registrants, including increased borrowings to temporarily finance related expenditures until recovery. The Duke Energy Registrants are working with various state commissions on the timing of recovery of these amounts. See Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, "Regulatory Matters" for more information.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P36 says fuel cost undercollections hurt cash flows and were financed with increased borrowings.
